provenance.instrument: City of Meadville Zoning Code (Part 13 Zoning Code, Title 1 Zoning, Ord. No. 3821 of 2-6-2024, as amended), as published on eCode360
provenance.status_detail: eCode360 ME4534, City of Meadville, Crawford County. Title 1 Zoning was adopted 2-6-2024 by Ord. No. 3821 and amended by Ord. No. 3824 (9-3-2024), 3831 and 3832 (4-15-2025), 3840 and 3841 (6-16-2026) and 3842 (7-7-2026), all folded into the text. The ADU rules of 1306.10(A) carry Ord. No. 3831. New Laws lists only Ord. No. 3846 (10-6-2026), which amends Article 327 (rental registration), not zoning. The use table (1303.05) and the bulk table (1303.06) are web text, not PDF attachments
provenance.code_current_through_note: eCode360: 'Includes legislation through 09-01-2026.' New Laws: Ord. No. 3846 (10-6-2026), rental registration only
checks: An accessory dwelling unit is a by-right use in R, MU-1 and MU-2 (Table 1303.05), under the standards of 1306.10(A)

An ADU is 'a dwelling unit that is structurally separated from, additional to, and subordinate to an existing principal dwelling on the same lot', and it counts as a principal use that creates mixed occupancy of a lot (1302.02)

A unit made inside or added onto the house is an 'accessory apartment' instead. The code treats it as converting the house to the next higher category, such as a two-family dwelling, once an independent household lives in it (1302.02). A two-family dwelling is by right in DPH, MU-1, MU-2, MU-3, I-S, I-C and GB-M, but not in R (Table 1303.05)
Only with a single-family detached house as the principal use, and only one ADU per lot (1306.10(A)(1), (2))

At least 401 sq ft of habitable floor area, and no more gross floor area than the house's habitable floor area. Not taller, wider at the frontage or larger in footprint than the house (1306.10(A)(4), (5))

A new ADU meets the district yards, height and clear distance for principal uses and may not sit in the front yard set by the house. A conversion of an existing structure is exempt if it does not expand further into a setback (1306.10(A)(6))
The ADU needs its own exclusive access to the outside (1306.10(A)(7))

Garages and sheds 'are prohibited from being used for living quarters or dwellings' (1306.19). The ADU rule allows the 'Conversion of an existing structure into an ADU' (1306.10(A)(6)). Ask whether a garage may be converted
No owner occupancy or family rule. No parking minimum: 'All uses are exempt from being required to provide a minimum number of automobile parking spaces' (1308.02(B))
The bulk table sets no lot coverage figure. Whether the ADU, as a second principal use, needs its own lot area is not said

A use not listed and not 'reasonably construed to be encompassed by one of the listed uses' is not permitted (1303.05(C)). The ADU is a listed use, so outside R, MU-1 and MU-2 the code does not permit it. In EDC an unlisted use may be a conditional use only if no other district lists it (1304.02(F)), so an ADU cannot use that path
A lot of record smaller than the minimum may hold a structure that conforms to the use rules, if it meets the yard and height rules (1307.02(A))

No section read bars a use variance. Variances need the five findings of 1311.08(H). The criteria of 1305.01 and 1305.02 that 1311.08(I) names for a use not listed are a procedure, not a path to an ADU
No parking or driveway between the house and the street, unless less than 12 ft is open between the house and a side line (1308.02(F)(2))
provenance.notes: Zoning office: City of Meadville, Zoning Administrator. Read in a browser on eCode360, one page at a time, on 2026-11-15, in print view. Searched the code (scope all) for accessory dwelling, in-law, accessory apartment, accessory suite, ECHO, elder cottage, granny, guest house, carriage house, tenant house, living quarters, second dwelling, conversion, two-family, caretaker, farm dwelling, family member and relative. Hits were 1303.05, 1306.10, the definitions of accessory apartment, dwelling, two-family dwelling and residential use, 1306.19, the sign articles and sections outside zoning. Read: Article 1302 (definitions, all but the sign terms in detail), Article 1303 (with Tables 1303.05 and 1303.06, checked column by column on screen), Article 1304, Article 1306 through 1306.25, Article 1307, Article 1308 and Article 1311. Not read: Article 1301, Article 1305 (special exception criteria), 1306.26 in part and 1306.27, Article 1309 (signs), Article 1310 (administration), Article 1312, Article 1315 and the zoning map. Table 1303.05 writes the districts as MU1, MU2, IS, IC and GBM. 1303.01 names them MU-1, MU-2, I-S, I-C and GB-M, the names used here. Height is measured from the average finished grade along all exterior walls to the highest point of the roof (1302.02). A 'guest house' is institutional lodging, not a home (1302.02), and is a special exception only in I-C.

term.note: 'A dwelling unit that is structurally separated from, additional to, and subordinate to an existing principal dwelling on the same lot. For the purposes of this title, ADUs shall be considered a principal use that creates mixed occupancy of a lot. Contrast with "accessory apartment."'

status.note: Uses noted with 'P' are permitted by right, regulated through the supplemental provisions. The ADU is P in R, MU-1 and MU-2. No family, owner or age rule

status_outside.note: Table 1303.05 lists the accessory dwelling unit as a use and permits it only in R, MU-1 and MU-2. Uses are permitted 'in accordance with the following provisions and tables' (1303.05(A)), so a blank cell means the use is not permitted there. The code does not permit an ADU in DPH, MU-3, I-S, I-C, GB-M or EDC. No section read bars a use variance, so a use variance from the Zoning Hearing Board is still a path to ask for

path.note: 'ADUs shall require permits in the same manner as a principal use.' A zoning permit when the standards of 1306.10(A) are met

fallback_path.note: Zoning Hearing Board on the five findings of 1311.08(H). No section read bars a use variance

value.name: Accessory apartment in or added to the house, which makes it a two-family dwelling
value.conditions: An accessory apartment is 'the conversion or expansion of any part of a dwelling into an additional dwelling unit that is structurally dependent on, conjoined with, and subordinate to, the existing dwelling'. It is treated as 'converting a dwelling to the next higher category of attached dwelling, such as a townhouse, duplex, or multifamily dwelling, at any time the apartment is let to or occupied by an independent household' (1302.02). A two-family dwelling ('a building comprised only of two dwelling units') is by right in these districts. A new two-family building in MU-1, MU-2, MU-3, DPH or GB-M needs a pitched roof, an entrance on each frontage and any garage behind the front face (1306.09(A)(2))
value.note: Not in R or EDC, which do not list a two-family dwelling. The code does not list an accessory apartment as a use of its own

value.name: Upper-floor residential above a nonresidential ground floor
value.conditions: 'A mixed use of a building where the ground floor is used for a permitted nonresidential use in the zoning district in which the building is located and a floor or floors above the ground floor are used for dwelling unit or residential use' (1302.02). Mixed-use buildings are permitted in all districts except R (1306.05)
value.note: The host is a building with a business or other nonresidential use on the ground floor, not a house alone

value.name: Cottage court (three or more cottages, duplexes or townhouses on one lot)
value.conditions: A group of three or more cottages, duplexes or banks of townhouses around a shared courtyard, access drive or driveway (1302.02), on a single undivided lot, at most seven buildings, each unit at least 401 sq ft of habitable floor area, at least 450 sq ft of open space per unit and a single access drive to a public road (1306.10(C))
value.note: A small development of three or more homes, not one added unit

building_types.note: 'ADUs shall only be permitted in conjunction with a single-family detached houses as the principal use.'

districts_read_no_listing.note: DPH, I-S and I-C permit single-family detached houses and two-family dwellings but no ADU. MU-3 and GB-M permit two-family dwellings and townhouses. EDC permits no dwelling except upper-floor residential

value.condition: Only with a single-family detached house as the principal use of the lot.
The ADU may not exceed the house in height, in width of frontage or in the gross area of its footprint.

The ADU needs its own exclusive access to the outside. A new ADU meets the yard, height and clear distance rules for principal buildings in the district, and no part of it may sit in the front yard set by the house.
Converting an existing structure into an ADU is exempt from the yard, height and clear distance rules, as long as the structure does not expand sideways further into a setback.

Garages and sheds 'are prohibited from being used for living quarters or dwellings'. A converted garage, or rooms over a garage, may be read as a garage used for living quarters. Ask the zoning officer.

types_allowed.note: An ADU is 'structurally separated from' the house. A unit inside the house or joined to it is an accessory apartment, which makes the house a two-family dwelling (see the alternatives). 1306.10(A)(6) speaks of 'Construction of new ADUs' and 'Conversion of an existing structure into an ADU'

min_sqft.note: 'ADUs shall have a minimum habitable floor area of 401 square feet.' Bathrooms, closets, halls and storage do not count as habitable floor area (1302.02 'Floor area')

value.part: habitable floor area (rooms for living, sleeping, eating or cooking, not bathrooms, closets, halls or storage)

max_share_of_part.note: 'ADUs shall have a maximum gross floor area of no greater than the habitable floor area of the principal dwelling.' The ADU's footprint also may not exceed the house's footprint (1306.10(A)(5))

value.what: an existing structure converted without further horizontal encroachment

exempt_building.note: 'Conversion of an existing structure into an ADU shall be exempt from these requirements so long as no horizontal expansion of the structure would encroach any further into an established setback.' The requirements are the district yards, height and clear distance for principal uses. The ADU still may not be taller than the house (1306.10(A)(5))

height_capped_at_house.note: 'ADUs shall not exceed the principal house in height, width of frontage, or gross area of footprint.'

district_yards_bind_accessory.note: 'Construction of new ADUs shall be subject to the minimum yard, height, clear distance, and setback requirements that apply to principal uses for the district.' A conversion of an existing structure is exempt if it does not expand further into a setback

front_yard_barred.note: 'No part of an ADU shall encroach into the front yard(s) established by the principal dwelling.' A front yard runs between the street right-of-way and the building line across the full width of the lot

unit_within_building_envelope.note: A new ADU meets the yards that apply to principal buildings in the district, so it stands inside the house's building envelope. No smaller rear yard on an alley

accessory_height_applies.note: A new ADU takes the height rule for principal uses in the district, and it may not be taller than the house. The code sets no separate height for accessory buildings

owner_occupancy.note: The ADU rules set no owner occupancy rule

family_only.note: The ADU rules set no family or age rule

max_adus.note: 'Only one ADU shall be permitted per lot.'

spaces_required.note: 'All uses are exempt from being required to provide a minimum number of automobile parking spaces unless otherwise provided by this Code' (Ord. No. 3842, 7-7-2026). Parking that is provided for a residential use goes on the same lot, except in MU-3 and DPH (1306.10(F))

min_lot_sqft.note: Width 35 ft, depth 60 ft. A lot of record smaller than this may still hold a structure that conforms to the use rules (1307.02(A))

setback_front_ft.note: Minimum 20 ft. Corner lots keep the front yard on every street (1302.02 'Lot line')

setback_side_ft.note: For buildings up to 20 ft tall. Each 5 ft of height above 20 ft adds 1 ft

setback_rear_ft.note: For buildings up to 20 ft tall. Each 5 ft of height above 20 ft adds 3 ft

principal_max_height_ft.note: Measured from the average finished grade along all exterior walls to the highest point of the roof (1302.02 'Height of building')

separation_ft.note: Clear distance between detached principal buildings up to 20 ft tall in R. Each 5 ft of height above 20 ft adds 1 ft. An ADU follows the clear distance for principal uses (1306.10(A)(6))

min_lot_sqft.note: Width 30 ft, depth 60 ft. Front yard within 5 ft of the average of the existing principal buildings on the block, but no closer to the street than the closest of them

setback_side_ft.note: For buildings up to 20 ft tall. Each 5 ft of height above 20 ft adds 1 ft

setback_rear_ft.note: For buildings up to 20 ft tall. Each 5 ft of height above 20 ft adds 3 ft

principal_max_height_ft.note: Measured from the average finished grade along all exterior walls to the highest point of the roof (1302.02 'Height of building')

separation_ft.note: Clear distance between detached principal buildings up to 20 ft tall. Each 5 ft of height above 20 ft adds 1 ft

min_lot_sqft.note: Width 25 ft, depth 60 ft. Front yard within 5 ft of the average of the existing principal buildings on the block, but no closer to the street than the closest of them

setback_side_ft.note: For buildings up to 20 ft tall. Each 5 ft of height above 20 ft adds 1 ft

setback_rear_ft.note: For buildings up to 20 ft tall. Each 5 ft of height above 20 ft adds 3 ft

principal_max_height_ft.note: Measured from the average finished grade along all exterior walls to the highest point of the roof (1302.02 'Height of building')

separation_ft.note: Clear distance between detached principal buildings up to 20 ft tall. Each 5 ft of height above 20 ft adds 1 ft
